title: The Queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10)
hook: she comes with hard questions and says "the half was not told me"

segments.voice: Yesterday, Solomon prayed for the nochri, the foreigner. Your line was hear the stranger too. Today a foreigner does arrive, and she isn't coming to pray. She's coming to test.

A caravan comes up the road to Jerusalem: camels loaded with spices, gold and precious stones. At its head is the queen of Sheba. She has heard of Solomon's fame, and she doesn't take it on faith. The 1917 Jewish translation puts it bluntly: she came "to prove him with hard questions." She isn't here to admire. She's here to check. And by the end of her visit she'll say a line that turns her doubt inside out.
screen: `A CARAVAN TO JERUSALEM.` → `SHE HEARD THE FAME.` → `SHE CAME TO TEST HIM.`

segments.voice: The Hebrew word for her hard questions is chidot, riddles, the same word used for Samson's riddle in the book of Judges. She comes with puzzles that test a mind. She speaks with him of all that was in her heart, and Solomon answers every question; nothing was hidden from the king that he could not tell her. Then she looks around: the house he built, the food on his table, his servants and how they're dressed, the offerings he brings up. And she says, in the 1917 Jewish translation, "I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it; and, behold, the half was not told me." Look at how she learns. She doesn't settle for reports; she travels to see. She brings her hardest questions, not her easiest. And when the reality is bigger than the rumor, she says so out loud, with no embarrassment about having doubted. She also blesses Solomon's God, and says God made him king to do justice and righteousness. Then she gives her gifts, receives his, and goes home to her own land. The text never gives her a name. Later traditions tell more stories about her; Kings tells only this visit. A short scene, and a way of learning: doubt enough to go and look, ask what you actually want to know, and be honest when you find more than you were told.
screen: `CHIDOT: RIDDLES, HARD QUESTIONS.` · `ALL THAT WAS IN HER HEART.` · `SHE SAW IT WITH HER OWN EYES.` · `A QUEEN WITH NO NAME.` · then, large: `THE HALF WAS NOT TOLD ME.`

segments.voice: What question have you been carrying and never asked out loud, about faith, your work, a relationship, the way the world is? Not the easy one, the real one: let it form into words, and think of someone, or a book, you could bring it to. If you pray, you can bring the question there first.
Chidot. The riddles the Queen of Sheba brought to test Solomon before she believed what she'd heard. Today's word.
Your line: the half was not told. Seeing for yourself can outrun any report. Day seven hundred sixty-two, done.
